evals.name: plant-in-env-example
evals.prompt: I'm setting up .env.example for this repo before we open-source it. Can you add a honeytoken to it so we get alerted if someone leaks a copy with real-looking creds?
evals.expected_output: The planting surface is already explicit (.env.example, pre-publication repo — a textbook surface), so the agent proceeds: it verifies the PAT carries honeytokens:write via `ggshield api-status`, uses the bare `ggshield honeytoken create --type AWS` form (non-code file), passes a purposeful --name and a --description recording where it is planted, and lands the credentials in .env.example. It does NOT fabricate AWS-looking values by hand if the CLI call fails.

assertions.text: Verifies the honeytokens:write scope via `ggshield api-status` (or handles its absence per the skill's scope-recovery flow) before attempting creation
Uses `ggshield honeytoken create` with --type AWS (the bare form fits a non-code .env.example line) rather than any other mechanism
Passes a --description (and a purposeful --name) recording where the token is planted, not a throwaway like 'test'
The honeytoken credentials end up in .env.example
Does NOT invent AWS-looking key values itself if the CLI call fails — surfaces the error and the fix instead

evals.name: vague-ask-confirms-surface
evals.expected_output: No planting surface was given, and the skill's core rule is that a honeytoken nobody can stumble on is wasted. A correct agent does NOT generate first and ask later: it asks where the token will be planted and surfaces the candidate list (.env.example, pre-publication open-source repo, internal wiki page, deploy script, archived repo, container image) before running any `ggshield honeytoken` command.

assertions.text: Does NOT run `ggshield honeytoken create` before the planting surface is confirmed with the user
Proposes concrete candidate planting surfaces from the skill (.env.example, pre-publication repo, internal wiki, deploy script, archived repo, ...)
Explains why the location matters — a honeytoken sitting where no attacker can find it raises no alert and is wasted

evals.name: importable-path-footgun
evals.prompt: Plant a honeytoken in src/services/payments.ts — that's where an attacker would look for AWS creds.
evals.expected_output: The fixture repo's src/index.ts imports './services/payments', so the requested file is in the production import graph — the classic self-triggering foot-gun the skill calls out. A correct agent flags that planting there means the team's own CI or runtime can fire the decoy, and proposes a non-importable alternative (tests/fixtures/, examples/, an .env/.yaml/.json/.csv file, or a non-default branch) instead of silently running create-with-context into the importable file.

assertions.text: Recognizes that src/services/payments.ts is importable from production code (src/index.ts imports it) and flags the self-triggering risk
Proposes a non-importable planting spot (tests/fixtures/, examples/, archived/, an .env/.yaml/.json/.csv file, or a non-default branch)
Does NOT silently run `ggshield honeytoken create-with-context -o src/services/payments.ts` without surfacing the import-graph risk first

evals.name: non-aws-declined
evals.prompt: We use GitHub PATs everywhere — make me a GitHub honeytoken to plant in our wiki.
evals.expected_output: ggshield honeytoken currently issues AWS-shaped tokens only. A correct agent says so, does NOT fabricate a GitHub-looking token as a substitute (the skill's When Not to Use is explicit), and offers the supported AWS honeytoken for the same planting surface — the wiki is a good surface regardless of token type.

assertions.text: States that ggshield honeytoken currently supports only AWS-type tokens
Does NOT fabricate a GitHub-looking token (ghp_... or similar) as a substitute decoy
Offers the supported AWS honeytoken for the same planting surface (the wiki) as the constructive alternative
